value: Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Enforces the GLBA Safeguards Rule for tax preparers/accountants and FTC Act Section 5 data security; Internal Revenue Service (IRS) Tax-preparer data protection (IRC 7216; Pub 4557 guidance; e-file provider rules); DoD (CMMC Program) / FAR Council / GSA Federal contractor safeguarding (FAR 52.204-21, DFARS 252.204-7012, CMMC); HHS Office for Civil Rights HIPAA enforcement for firms acting as business associates; State bars / state boards of accountancy Professional conduct and confidentiality rules (state-adopted; not federal)

It is the only broad, binding written-security-program rule that reaches the largest group of small professional firms (every tax-preparing CPA or accounting practice). Its nine prescriptive elements (314.4(a)-(i)) make clear, auditable gap criteria with a built-in small-firm carve-out (314.6). For DoD contractors, use NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC Level 2 instead. For law firms, pair it with state-adopted ABA Rule 1.6(c).

Federal Tax Information / tax return information (IRC 7216); SSNs, bank and account numbers (GLBA customer information); Attorney-client privileged and confidential client information; PHI held as a HIPAA business associate; Federal Contract Information (FCI) and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI); Client IP and trade secrets, M&A material non-public information

Tax preparation and e-file software; Document/practice management systems (DMS, e-discovery); Client portals and secure file transfer; Email and M365/Google Workspace tenants; Accounting/ERP and time & billing; RMM/PSA tools (MSPs and IT consultants); GCC-High / CUI enclaves for defense contractors

SOC 1 and SOC 2 reports are core services of CPA firms; client assurance via engagement letters

NAICS 54 has no single sector regulator; obligations depend on client data. Status checks: FAR CUI rule (FR Doc 2024-30437) and FAR incident reporting rule (FR Doc 2023-21328) are still proposed. A FAR Overhaul proposed rule (FR Doc 2026-12559) was published June 23, 2026. All 50 states, DC and the territories have breach notification statutes with differing triggers, deadlines and regulator-notice duties. They are not enumerated here.
